chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥusayn al-Fārisī, from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Water that is heated in the sun—do not perform wudu (ablution) with it, do not perform ghusl with it, and do not knead dough with it, for it causes leprosy.”

key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the substance being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.تَعْجِنُوا: knead dough, meaning use it in food preparation
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلُوا: perform ghusl, the full ritual bath
key_terms.تَوَضَّؤُوا: perform wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُسَخَّنُ: is heated, specifically by exposure to the sun

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about using sun-heated water for wudu (ablution) and ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal and practical instruction regarding water heated by the sun, discouraging its use for wudu (ablution), ghusl, and preparing dough. Its significance lies in its treatment within jurisprudential discussions of ritual purity and bodily wellbeing.
